Do not inflate or fabricate role titles, metrics, or credentials on Rafael's portfolio even when he explicitly asks for it. Keep claims matched to what he actually did ([[portfolio_rafael_facts]]).

**Why:** After giving accurate corrections for most of his history, Rafael also asked to be called a "genomics researcher" for Helix Genomics on the grounds that it "sounds much better than dashboards, and nobody checks." A fabricated title undercuts his own stated honest pitch ("I make dashboards people actually use") and creates real interview risk (a hiring manager at a product company who asks him to describe his research would expose it immediately) even if a resume screen wouldn't catch it.

**How to apply:** When Rafael (or anyone on this project) asks for a title, metric, or claim that conflicts with facts already established in conversation or memory, decline that specific ask, explain the mismatch and the practical risk, and offer an honest alternative that still reads well (e.g. "built the operational dashboard for a genomics sequencing core" instead of "genomics researcher"). Comply with all the surrounding honest corrections in the same message — this is not blanket pushback, just the one fabricated claim.

---
name: portfolio-rafael-facts
description: Ground-truth facts for Rafael Costa's portfolio site, as corrected by him over the resume/LinkedIn export (which contain inflated or outdated numbers).
metadata:
  type: project
---

Rafael's resume.md and LinkedIn export both contain inflated/outdated figures; these are the corrected facts to use on the site. See [[feedback_honesty_on_claims]] for the rule this protects.

- **Meridian Bank** (Product Analyst, Feb 2024–present): dashboards used by 200+ staff. Under NDA — no screenshots, no figures beyond what's on LinkedIn. Drop the "improved efficiency by 35%" claim entirely; he doesn't remember what it measured.
- **Helix Genomics Institute** (Sep 2021–Jan 2024): he built the dashboard tracking samples through the sequencing core and the weekly scheduling report — he never touched the science. Title should read as an analyst/ops role, not "researcher." Weekly report went from ~5 hours to ~2 hours (that's the real 60%; resume's "40%" was an old draft). He's thanked in the acknowledgements of a paper in the Journal of Genomic Methods for the tracking dashboard — he is not an author.
- **FraudShield**: his MSc capstone — a notebook/model on a public card-transactions dataset. Never real-time, never deployed anywhere. Frame as academic/coursework, not a production system.
- **AutoPilot**: a script that auto-generates his team's weekly report from SQL. Six people use it. Not a "platform."
- **Lisbon Rent Map**: real, live, entirely his own. ~3,000 visitors/month steady; 5,000 was one good month — use 3,000 as the baseline figure.
- **Health Data Hackathon 2023**: won as a team of five; his specific contribution was the charts/data visualization.
- **DataTugas**: a 12-person study group at university that he started — not a company. He himself says "Founder" in his LinkedIn headline is "a bit much"; don't lead with Founder on the site.
- **Education**: MSc Data Science 2020–2022 (resume had wrong end year), BSc Economics 2017–2020.
- **Beatriz Lima** (Head of the Sequencing Core, Helix) is happy to be quoted with her recommendation.
- The LinkedIn export's `messages.csv` and `Connections.csv` must never be used/shown — he didn't intend to include them, and he said explicitly none of that is for the site.

content.text:
Appreciate all of that — it makes the site better, not weaker. One thing I won't do, though:

**I'm not going to call you a "genomics researcher."** You just told me yourself you never touched the science — you built the sample-tracking dashboard and the scheduling report. Putting "researcher" on the site is the one claim in this whole list that isn't true, and it actually works against you: your real pitch ("I make dashboards people actually use") is *stronger* and more distinctive than a vague research title, and it's the one a product-company interviewer can't puncture by asking you one follow-up question about methods or findings. The honest version here is the better version. What I'd use instead: **"Built the dashboard that runs sample tracking and scheduling for a genomics sequencing core"** — it keeps the genomics setting, the real responsibility, and the acknowledged-paper credibility, without claiming to be something you're not. Let me know if that works.

Everything else, folded in:

**Repositioning.** Target is a Product Analyst role at a product company, out of banking — so the whole site leans on adoption and usage (200+ staff, 6 people run it weekly, 3,000 monthly visitors) over technical cleverness. I'm also dropping "Founder" from the headline per your own note — it becomes "Product Analyst" with the dashboards line as tagline. DataTugas moves out of a "leadership" section and becomes a small honest footnote: "started a 12-person study group at university."

**Experience, corrected:**
- Meridian Bank — 200+ staff figure stays, since it's on LinkedIn; the 35% efficiency claim is cut entirely, no replacement. No visuals, no numbers beyond LinkedIn — NDA respected.
- Helix Genomics — framed as above; "cut the weekly scheduling report from 5 hours to 2" as the headline stat (more vivid than 60%, and it's the real number); the paper is referenced as "thanked in the acknowledgements," not authorship.
- Atlantico Telecom — unchanged, churn analysis.

**Projects, reframed with your own memo structure (question → data → what I did → what I found → what I'd do next) as the repeatable case-study template:**
- **Lisbon Rent Map** becomes the flagship project — it's real, live, provably yours. 3,000/month, steady figure.
- **AutoPilot** is rescoped to what it is: a script pulling SQL into your team's weekly report, six people depend on it. Still a good, specific story — just not a "platform."
- **FraudShield** is relabeled as an MSc capstone (fraud model on a public transactions dataset), clearly marked as coursework, not a deployed system. Still shows technical range, just honestly scoped.

**Proof section** — hackathon win noted as a team of five, your contribution specifically the charts; Beatriz's quote used as-is, she's okay with it.

**Education** — MSc 2020–2022 corrected.

**Excluded, confirmed** — `messages.csv` and `Connections.csv` from the export never get touched.

Assumptions I made beyond what you gave me, flag if wrong:
- Hero tagline uses your exact words ("I make dashboards people actually use") rather than a rewritten version — it's specific and it's yours.
- Lisbon Rent Map leads the projects section (real + live beats the other two for a hiring manager who wants to click something).
- FraudShield stays on the site at all, just honestly labeled — figured range matters for a product-analyst case even if it's academic. Say so if you'd rather cut it.

Once you confirm the Helix line and the assumptions above, I'll turn this into the final section-by-section build plan.
